text: Meanwhile the first stranger quietly returned. <break time="0.8s" /> To the empty cottage. <break time="0.8s" /> And soon the hangman came back too. <break time="0.8s" /> So the two ate and drank together. <break time="0.8s" /> Before parting. <break time="0.8s" /> Out on the hills. <break time="0.8s" /> The searchers at last found the little man. <break time="0.8s" /> Standing quietly near a tree. <break time="0.8s" /> And he calmly allowed himself. <break time="0.8s" /> To be taken back. <break time="0.8s" /> But at the cottage. <break time="0.8s" /> Two officers from the jail. <break time="0.8s" /> Looked at him and declared. <break time="0.8s" /> That this was not the escaped prisoner at all. <break time="0.8s" /> But a completely different man. <break time="0.8s" /> The little man then explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was the prisoners brother. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had been walking to Casterbridge. <break time="0.8s" /> To see him for the last time. <break time="0.8s" /> When he had looked into the cottage. <break time="0.8s" /> And seen his brother sitting beside the hangman. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been so shocked. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could only run away. <break time="0.8s" /> Only then did everyone realize. <break time="0.8s" /> That the quiet man by the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had sung so cheerfully with the hangman. <break time="0.8s" /> Had been the escaped prisoner himself. <break time="0.8s" /> The search went on for days. <break time="0.8s" /> But the country people pitied the poor man. <break time="0.8s" /> So he was never caught. <break time="0.8s" /> And his story is still told. <break time="0.8s" /> In Wessex today. <break time="0.8s" /> Shepherd Fennel and his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Have long since died. <break time="0.8s" /> And the baby whose christening they celebrated that night. <break time="0.8s" /> Is now a woman growing old herself.
